# Carousel

Header: `winui/ui/navigation/Carousel.hpp`. Spec: `winui/ui/navigation/Carousel.hpp`.

Shows one item at a time, filling the whole view, and flips between them with previous/next buttons, the mouse wheel or the keyboard.

Items are any elements, owned by the view ([add_item()](#add_item)). They sit side by side along the flip axis, each the size of the view. Only the items in view are drawn or get input, and [Tab](tabs.md#uitab) reaches only the selected item's focusable content. The previous/next buttons appear while the mouse moves over the view and for 3 s after, or once keyboard focus arrives. A button never shows on a side with no item beyond it. One wheel turn flips one item. Along the flip axis the arrow keys and PageUp/PageDown step one item, and Home/End jump to the ends. A step to a neighbor slides over 300 ms, and longer jumps land at once. For a page indicator, pair it with a [PipsPager](pips-pager.md#uipipspager) bound to the same index.

Example: 
```cpp
// Declarative: the pages are children, each filling the view.
ui::Property<std::size_t> page{0};
window.set_content(ui::VerticalStack{
    .spacing  = 8,
    .content  = {
        ui::Carousel{
            .selected_index = page,
            .height         = 270.0f,
            .max_width      = 400.0f,
            .content        = {
                ui::Image{.source = ui::Bitmap::read("cliff.jpg")},
                ui::Image{.source = ui::Bitmap::read("grapes.jpg")},
                ui::Text{.text = "The end", .horizontal_alignment = ui::Alignment::Center},
            },
        },
        ui::PipsPager{.selected_index = page, .number_of_pages = 3}, // two-way
    },
});

// Imperative.
auto  stack = std::make_unique<ui::StackControl>(ui::Orientation::Vertical);
auto* flip  = stack->add(std::make_unique<ui::CarouselControl>());
flip->set_height(200.0f);
flip->add_item(std::make_unique<ui::TextControl>("First")); // becomes the selection
flip->add_item(std::make_unique<ui::TextControl>("Second"));
flip->on_selection_changed([&page](std::size_t i) { page = i; });
flip->set_selected_index(1); // slides once laid out; fires the handler
```

## `ui::Carousel`

One item at a time, flipped with arrows, the wheel or the keys. Builds a [ui::CarouselControl](#uicarouselcontrol). Its items are child elements, and each fills the whole view.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Property<std::size_t> page{0};

window.set_content(ui::Carousel{
    .selected_index = page,
    .height         = 270.0f,
    .max_width      = 400.0f,
    .content        = {
        ui::Image{.source = ui::Bitmap::read("cliff.jpg")},
        ui::Image{.source = ui::Bitmap::read("grapes.jpg")},
        ui::Text{.text = "The end", .horizontal_alignment = ui::Alignment::Center},
    },
});
```

Every field, in the order a designated initializer names them:

```cpp
ui::Carousel{
    .selected_index, .orientation, .use_animations, .background, .border_brush,
    .border_thickness, .style, .margin, .width, .height, .min_width, .min_height, .max_width,
    .max_height, .horizontal_alignment, .vertical_alignment, .visible, .tool_tip, .enabled,
    .accessibility, .on_selection_changed, .on_pointer_entered, .on_pointer_exited,
    .on_got_focus, .on_lost_focus, .on_key_down, .on_wheel, .control, .content
}
```

Fields, in declaration order (designators must follow it):

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <span id="uicarousel-selected_index"></span>`selected_index` | `ui::TwoWayField<std::size_t>` | `{0}` | The index of the item in view. |
| <span id="uicarousel-orientation"></span>`orientation` | `ui::Binding<ui::Orientation>` | `{ui::Orientation::Horizontal}` | Horizontal (the default) flips left/right; Vertical flips up/down. |
| <span id="uicarousel-use_animations"></span>`use_animations` | `ui::Binding<bool>` | `{true}` | One-item flips slide. |
| <span id="uicarousel-background"></span>`background` | `ui::Binding<ui::Paint>` |  | The fill behind the items: a fixed color or a theme resource; unset is the window's background color. |
| <span id="uicarousel-border_brush"></span>`border_brush` | `ui::Binding<ui::Paint>` |  | A border drawn over the items' edges: a fixed color or a theme resource; unset draws none. |
| <span id="uicarousel-border_thickness"></span>`border_thickness` | `ui::Binding<ui::Thickness>` |  | See [`border_brush`](#uicarousel-border_brush). |
| <span id="uicarousel-on_selection_changed"></span>`on_selection_changed` | `ui::Callback<void(std::size_t)>` |  | Called with the index of the item now in view. A bound value doesn't run it. |
| <span id="uicarousel-on_pointer_entered"></span>`on_pointer_entered` | `ui::Action` |  | The pointer moved onto the control. |
| <span id="uicarousel-on_pointer_exited"></span>`on_pointer_exited` | `ui::Action` |  | The pointer left the control. |
| <span id="uicarousel-on_got_focus"></span>`on_got_focus` | `ui::Action` |  | Keyboard focus arrived on the control, or on anything inside it, from outside it. A control with nothing focusable in it never gets focus, and never raises this. |
| <span id="uicarousel-on_lost_focus"></span>`on_lost_focus` | `ui::Action` |  | Keyboard focus left the control and everything inside it. |
| <span id="uicarousel-on_key_down"></span>`on_key_down` | `ui::Callback<ui::Handling(const ui::KeyEvent&)>` |  | A key pressed while focus is on the control or inside it, before the control's own handling; [ui::Handled](../core/namespace-ui.md#handled) stops it there ([Element::on_key_down()](../tree/element.md#on_key_down)). |
| <span id="uicarousel-on_wheel"></span>`on_wheel` | `ui::Callback<ui::Handling(const ui::PointerEvent&)>` |  | A wheel turn over the control, before the control scrolls; [ui::Handled](../core/namespace-ui.md#handled) stops it there ([Element::on_wheel()](../tree/element.md#on_wheel)). |
| <span id="uicarousel-control"></span>`control` | `ui::ControlOut<ui::Carousel>` |  | Out: the handle that receives the built control. |
| <span id="uicarousel-content"></span>`content` | `ui::SpecList` |  | The pages, in flip order; each fills the whole view. |

## `ui::CarouselControl`

Derives from `ui::Element`, `ui::SelectionProvider`.

Shows one item at a time, filling the whole view, and flips between them with previous/next buttons, the mouse wheel or the keyboard.

Items are any elements, owned by the view ([add_item()](#add_item)). They sit side by side along the flip axis, each the size of the view. Only the items in view are drawn or get input, and [Tab](tabs.md#uitab) reaches only the selected item's focusable content. The previous/next buttons appear while the mouse moves over the view and for 3 s after, or once keyboard focus arrives. A button never shows on a side with no item beyond it. One wheel turn flips one item. Along the flip axis the arrow keys and PageUp/PageDown step one item, and Home/End jump to the ends. A step to a neighbor slides over 300 ms, and longer jumps land at once. For a page indicator, pair it with a [PipsPager](pips-pager.md#uipipspager) bound to the same index.

### CarouselControl

```cpp
CarouselControl() = default
```

An empty view: no items, nothing selected, not focusable.

### add_item

```cpp
template <typename T>
T* add_item(std::unique_ptr<T> item)
```

Append an item, taking ownership; returns a non-owning observer. The first item added becomes the selection (without firing [on_selection_changed()](#on_selection_changed)).

### item_count

```cpp
std::size_t item_count() const
```

How many items the view holds.

### item

```cpp
Element* item(std::size_t index) const
```

The item at `index` (owned by the view), or nullptr past the end.

### selected_index

```cpp
std::optional<std::size_t> selected_index() const
```

The index of the item in view; unset with no items.

### set_selected_index

```cpp
void set_selected_index(std::size_t index)
```

Selects the item at `index`, clamped to the items there are. A change fires on_selection_changed. A step to a neighbor slides ([use_animations()](#use_animations)), and anything else lands at once. Ignored with no items, since a carousel with items always shows one.

### orientation

```cpp
Orientation orientation() const
```

The flip axis; Horizontal by default.

### set_orientation

```cpp
void set_orientation(Orientation orientation)
```

Changes the flip axis and which arrow keys flip; updates the layout.

### use_animations

```cpp
bool use_animations() const
```

Whether a one-item flip slides. On by default.

### set_use_animations

```cpp
void set_use_animations(bool animate)
```

Turns the one-item slide on or off for later flips.

### set_background

```cpp
void set_background(Paint color)
```

The fill behind the items: a fixed color or a theme resource. Empty, the default, is the window's background color.

### set_border_brush

```cpp
void set_border_brush(Paint color)
```

The border color around the items (none by default), drawn over their edges.

### set_border_thickness

```cpp
void set_border_thickness(const Thickness& thickness)
```

The border's thickness per side, DIPs (0 by default). Drawn over the items, so it does not shrink them; redraws only.

### on_selection_changed

```cpp
void on_selection_changed(Callback<void(std::size_t)> handler)
```

Called with the new index whenever the selected item changes, by a button, the wheel, a key or [set_selected_index()](#set_selected_index). One handler; setting another replaces it.

### previous_button_visible

```cpp
bool previous_button_visible() const
```

Whether the previous/next buttons are showing right now (see the class comment).

### next_button_visible

```cpp
bool next_button_visible() const
```

As [previous_button_visible()](#previous_button_visible), for the next button.

### previous_button_bounds

```cpp
Rect previous_button_bounds() const
```

Where the previous button sits (window DIPs): 16x38 centered 1 DIP inside the left edge, or 38x16 at the top when vertical. Valid after [arrange()](../tree/element.md#arrange), shown or not.

### next_button_bounds

```cpp
Rect next_button_bounds() const
```

As [previous_button_bounds()](#previous_button_bounds), at the right (or bottom) edge.

### focusable

```cpp
bool focusable() const override
```

Focusable while enabled and holding at least one item.

### focused

```cpp
bool focused() const
```

Whether the view itself holds keyboard focus.

### for_each_child

```cpp
void for_each_child(ChildVisitor visit) const override
```

Every item, in order.

### collect_focusables

```cpp
void collect_focusables(std::vector<Element*>& out) override
```

The view itself, then the selected item's focusable descendants. [Tab](tabs.md#uitab) cannot reach the other items.

### automation_role

```cpp
AutomationRole automation_role() const override
```

A List.

### measure_override

```cpp
Size measure_override(Size available, const MeasureContext& context) const override
```

Takes the whole available size on a bounded axis; on an unbounded one, the largest item's.

### arrange_override

```cpp
void arrange_override(const Rect& final_rect, const ArrangeContext& context) override
```

Gives every item the view's size and places them along the flip axis at the current position.

### render_override

```cpp
void render_override(Renderer& renderer, const RenderContext& context) const override
```

Draws the background, the items in view (clipped), the border, the buttons while shown and the focus ring, which sits just inside the bounds.

### pointer_override

```cpp
bool pointer_override(const PointerEvent& e) override
```

Mouse movement shows the buttons; a click on a button flips. Other input reaches the items in view.

### wheel_override

```cpp
bool wheel_override(const PointerEvent& e) override
```

An item in view that scrolls gets the turn first. Otherwise each turn flips one item, and a repeat in the same direction within 200 ms is ignored. Returns false (not handled) at the first or last item and for Ctrl+wheel, so an outer scroller can react.

### hit_test_children

```cpp
void hit_test_children(Point p, std::vector<Element*>& out) const override
```

The children `p` (in this element's layout coordinates) is tested against, topmost first. Default: what [for_each_child()](#for_each_child) lists, last first. A container that draws in another order ([Panel](../layout/panel.md#uipanel)'s z-index), a control with parts [for_each_child()](#for_each_child) does not list, or one whose parts cover others in places (a pane drawn over the content) lists them here.

### covers_children_at

```cpp
bool covers_children_at(Point p) const override
```

Whether a part of this element drawn over its children is at `p` (a scroll bar over the content), so the element is hit there instead of a child. Default: false.

### children_hit_clip

```cpp
std::optional<Rect> children_hit_clip() const override
```

Where the children can be hit, in this element's layout coordinates, or nullopt for anywhere (the default): a scrolling control returns its viewport, so content scrolled out of view is not hit.

### tick_override

```cpp
void tick_override(Duration delta) override
```

Advances the slide and the buttons' show timer, then ticks the items.

### enabled_changed

```cpp
void enabled_changed() override
```

[is_enabled()](../tree/element.md#is_enabled) flipped, through [set_enabled()](../tree/element.md#set_enabled) here or on an ancestor, or a move to another parent. Drop any press or hover state. The element is redrawn either way. No-op by default.

### key_override

```cpp
bool key_override(const KeyEvent& e) override
```

Arrows along the flip axis step, Home/End jump to the ends, PageUp/PageDown step one item.

### focus_changed

```cpp
void focus_changed(bool focused) override
```

Called by [Window](../tree/window.md); gaining keyboard focus ([focus_visible()](../tree/element.md#focus_visible)) shows the buttons. Redraws.

### focus_ring_inside

```cpp
bool focus_ring_inside() const override
```

Inside the view, which fills its slot edge to edge.
